(“Viridian” or the “Company”) reports additional near-surface copper-nickel-cobalt mineralization at its Kraken project in Labrador, including 21.2 metres at 0.62% CuEq in an extension of hole VKS25-026. The latest results continue to demonstrate broad, consistent mineralization across Kraken Main, with assays pending from 16 additional holes, including holes with substantial visually identified sulphide-rich intervals.
Hole VKS25-026E returned 21.2 metres grading 0.62% CuEq, extending previously reported mineralization.

Hole VKS25-057 returned 24.45 metres at 0.18% CuEq within the mineralized halo overlying the main sulphide accumulation. Assays remain pending from the final 21 metres, which contain most of the visually identified patchy net-textured sulphides, with only the final 5 metres of the reported interval intersecting the upper portion of this mineralization.
Additional holes returned 43.05 metres grading 0.16% CuEq and 23.3 metres grading 0.20% CuEq, supporting the widespread distribution of mineralization across Kraken Main.

Following the closing of a first tranche of financing for proceeds of $5.77 million, Viridian is preparing for its maiden resource drilling program, with 16 holes still awaiting assay results and an updated Exploration Target planned for January 2027.
Tyrell Sutherland, President and CEO of Viridian Metals, commented:

“The consistency of broad mineralization beginning almost at surface continues to be one of Kraken's most compelling attributes. These latest results suggest that substantial mineralized halos may extend beyond the main sulphide accumulation, potentially adding significant scale to an already large system. With much of our 2026 drilling still awaiting assays, we believe we are only beginning to establish the full extent of Kraken Main.

“Following our recently completed $5.77 million financing, we are fully funded for our 2027 maiden resource drilling program. Our focus is now shifting toward establishing the scale of the resource and evaluating how Kraken's near-surface geometry and substantial mineralized thicknesses could translate into a large-scale, low-cost mining operation.”

Drilling Continues to Demonstrate Broad, Consistent Near-Surface Mineralization

The latest assay results (Table 1) continue to demonstrate broad, near-surface mineralization across Kraken Main. The results include an extension of previously reported mineralization in VKS25-026, which returned a total interval of 21.2 metres grading 0.62% CuEq from top of bedrock at 5.05 metres depth. Additional results include 43.05 metres grading 0.16% CuEq in VKS26-052 and 23.3 metres grading 0.20% CuEq in VKS25-059, in both cases from top of bedrock beneath less than 3 metres of overburden.

Partial assays from VKS25-057 returned 24.45 metres grading 0.18% CuEq from the top of bedrock at 1.45 metres depth, including 5.9 metres grading 0.28% CuEq, with the highest grades at the base of the reported interval. This interval was logged as disseminated sulphides, with an average assay-derived sulphide content of 4.3% and is interpreted as a mineralized halo overlying the main sulphide accumulation (Figure 1). The remaining 21 metres contain long intervals of patchy net-textured sulphides, indicating that the principal sulphide accumulation lies within the interval awaiting assays.

The results from VKS25-057 suggest that broad halos of lower-grade mineralization may surround the principal mineralized horizon. Other broad, lower-grade intersections, including 43.05 metres grading 0.16% CuEq in VKS26-052, may similarly represent mineralized halos above or below the main sulphide accumulation rather than the principal horizon itself. Further drilling and geological interpretation are required to establish these relationships.

The potential presence of broad mineralized halos surrounding the principal sulphide accumulation could increase the scale of the bulk-tonnage opportunity at Kraken Main. Given the near-surface geometry of the system, additional mineralized intervals have favourable implications for potential strip ratios and mining costs. A larger mineralized envelope would provide greater flexibility in mine planning, with the potential to optimize production rates and operating margins.

The 2026 drill program was designed to establish the continuity of near-surface mineralization across Kraken Main and demonstrate consistent mineralized thicknesses exceeding 30 metres, more than three times the average thickness identified by the initial Exploration Target (see news release dated September 15, 2026, available on the Company's SEDAR+ profile at

). The latest results complement previously reported mineralized intervals exceeding 50 metres, providing further evidence of a broad mineralized system extending across widely separated portions of the Main Zone.

With assays outstanding from 16 additional holes, including substantial intervals of visually identified patchy net-textured sulphides along the southern extension of Kraken Main, significant portions of the 2026 drilling program remain to be evaluated. The broad distribution of near-surface mineralization continues to support the Company's bulk-tonnage exploration model, while the remaining results will help establish the grade, thickness and continuity of mineralization ahead of the planned January 2027 Exploration Target update.

True thickness of the reported mineralized intervals is not yet known. Reported interval lengths represent downhole core lengths and should not be interpreted as true thickness.

Intercepts are calculated using a 0.1% CuEq¹ cut-off grade corresponding to approximately US$10 NSR with no more than 5 m of internal dilution. Viridian has completed specific gravity measurements and full multi-element geochemical analysis on all samples to support ongoing characterization of the Kraken system.

The holes reported in this release were prioritized for laboratory analysis in October. Additional samples from holes VKS26-061, VKS26-063-70, and VKS25-057E, which were drilled along the 4.5km length of the Main Zone have been delivered to Activation Laboratories Ltd. (“Activation Labs”) in Ancaster, Ontario, with assays pending. Additional holes VKS26-071-74 and extension holes VKS25-041e, VKS25-042e, and VKS25-046e have been processed and will be delivered to the lab in the coming days. All assays from the remaining 16 holes are expected to be received by the end of the year.

Results also remain outstanding from holes spaced approximately 500 metres apart along a further 2.5 kilometres of Kraken Main to the south, including previously reported visually identified patchy net-textured sulphide intervals of 41.8 and 47.3 metres. Laboratory assays are required to establish the grades of these intervals.

Viridian completed 33 drill holes during its 2026 exploration program. Both rigs have been mobilized off site and the Company’s focus will now shift to reporting results, metallurgical analysis and interpretation in preparation for an update to the Exploration Target in January 2027. The Company has issued initial requests for proposals (RFPs) for its 2027 resource drilling program.
Table 2 – Kraken Main Zone 2026 drill collars. Collar coordinates are reported in NAD83 / UTM Zone 20N. Azimuths are referenced to true north. Bold holes are included in this release.

On receipt from the drill site BTW-sized drill core was systematically logged for geological attributes, photographed and sampled at Viridian’s Core Shack at Kraken Camp. Sample lengths as small as 0.30 m were used to isolate features of interest, but most samples within moderate to strong mineralization were 0.5-1.0 m in length. Core was cut in half lengthwise along a pre-determined line, with one half (same half, consistently, dictated by cut line where present) collected for analysis and one half stored as a record. Standard reference materials and blanks were inserted by Viridian personnel at regular intervals into the sample stream. Bagged samples were sealed with security tags to ensure integrity during transport. They were delivered by expeditor to Activation Labs’ facility in Ancaster, ON.

Activation Labs is independent of Viridian and accredited to ISO/IEC 17025. Samples (up to 7 kg) were dried and crushed to 80% passing 2 mm, then riffle split (250 g) and pulverized to 95% passing 105 µm (code RX1). A four-acid near-total digest with an inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectroscopy (ICP-OES) finish was used for 35-element analysis on 25 g sample pulps (code 1F2). Samples that were over the analyses limit for Co, Cu and Ni were reanalyzed using sodium peroxide fusion ICP (code 8-peroxide).

Tyrell Sutherland, P.Geo., President and CEO of Viridian Metals and a Qualified Person as defined in National Instrument 43-101 - Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects, has reviewed and approved the technical disclosure contained in this news release. Mr. Sutherland is not independent of the Company.

CuEq¹ calculated based on the following metal prices (USD): $4.00/lb Cu, $7.50/lb Ni and $15.00/lb Co, and a recovery of 80% for Ni and Co, consistent with comparable projects. The Company believes that all metals included in the CuEq¹ calculation have a reasonable potential to be recovered. CuEq¹ values are provided for illustrative purposes only; actual recoveries and metal prices may differ materially from those assumed.
